title: Symmetric backpressure recovery and ghost-output pruning for interrupted generations
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Investigate and implement a symmetric backpressure recovery mechanism that consistently prunes 'ghost' partial outputs left behind when clients disconnect mid-generation, while preserving resumability for healthy clients. This addresses intermittent customer reports of stale partial drafts showing in console traces and metric inflation of inflight tokens.
proposed_solution: Introduce a symmetric two-stage reclaim protocol: (1) soft-quarantine: when a disconnect or client timeout occurs, mark generations as quarantined and stop scheduling for CPU/GPU work; (2) reclamation sweep: after a configurable grace window, run eviction that prunes ephemeral prefixes and releases KV-cache, with metadata tombstone that prevents accidental resumptions. Provide an opt-in resumable flag to skip reclamation for long-lived clients.
technical_details: New state enum for generations: ACTIVE, QUIARANTINED, HELD_RESUMABLE, EVICTED
Add generation metadata: last_seen_timestamp, disconnect_cause(enum), resumable_flag(bool), prefetch_tokens_count(int)
Soft-quarantine is triggered on TCP/HTTP client disconnect, SDK-level abort, or SLO timeout. Soft-quarantine stops scheduling further decoding and marks KV entries as low-priority for eviction.
Reclamation sweep runs in two phases: fast-pass (metadata-only) to identify candidates, slow-pass to safely free KV cache and GPU scratch memory. Fast-pass marks tombstone with eviction_eta.
Introduce 'grace_window_ms' per-tenant with default 30000ms and per-request override through streaming.options.resumable_grace_ms.
Compat shim: for older SDKs without resumable_flag, default to existing behavior but expose metric 'compat_resumable_implicit' for telemetry.
Metrics to emit: quarantined_generations, reclaimed_generations, successful_resumes, reclaimed_kv_bytes, average_reclaim_latency
API change: add 'resume_token' durability guarantee when resumable_flag is set; otherwise resume attempts return soft error with reason 'reclaimed'.
acceptance_criteria: Partial generations from abrupt disconnects are no longer visible in streaming console traces after reclamation window unless resumable_flag is used
Metrics show reduction in sustained inflight token counts by >15% for tenants with noisy disconnect patterns
Resume flow successfully restores generations when resumable_flag=true within grace window in 99% of tests
No regression in tail-latency for live streaming requests (SLO: p99 latency increase < 3%)
Compatibility tests pass for SDKs v1.0 through v1.4; older SDKs default behavior unchanged
implementation_plan: Design doc + simulation (week 1): microbench KV eviction under quarantine scenarios
Core runtime changes (week 2): implement generation state transition and metadata storage
Controller sweep job (week 3): implement fast-pass and slow-pass reclaimers with safety checks
SDK opt-in (week 3): expose resumable flag and resume_token handling in Node/Python SDKs
QA and chaos testing (week 4): run disconnect fuzzing, simulated network partitions, and function_call-heavy workloads
Rollout (week 5): gradual traffic ramp, feature flag per-tenant, monitor metrics and rollback on anomalies
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-eager eviction may drop content users expect to resume. Mitigation: default conservative grace_window, and per-tenant override via Console.
Risk: KV-cache churn increases resource pressure. Mitigation: slow-pass reclaimer throttled by mempressure signal and prioritize low-cost evictions.

Risk: Interaction with tool/function calls may leave external tool side-effects inconsistent. Mitigation: ensure quarantine prevents tool re-invocations and mark instrumented tool-calls as idempotent where possible; include logs for operators.
qa_steps: Unit tests for generation state transitions and tombstone semantics
Integration tests: simulate client disconnect at multiple decode steps and assert reclaim behavior
End-to-end: reproduce customer-reported scenario from incident INC-2026-03-02 and verify cleanup
Load test: measure p99 latency and reclaim throughput under 200k concurrent streams
